title: Inside cover and first page: entries 554, 642, 647 of 1837

entries.from: Bishop Joannes, Szatmár
entries.abstract: Károly Werfer, bookseller of Kassa (Košice), is printing a Hungarian edition of a French work, "A friendly examination of the English Church and of the Reformation in general". The bishop urges the clergy to subscribe and wants at least one copy bought for each district. Names of subscribers are due by the start of August. Countersigned as revised by the vice-archdeacon.

entries.abstract: Arising from the conversion of Carolus Vajna, a Unitarian from the Transylvanian diocese: because the form of Unitarian baptism is in doubt, such converts are to be baptised conditionally.

entries.from: Bishop Joannes
entries.abstract: Passes on a Lieutenancy Council notice of 11 July (no. 21502) about the Institute for the Blind in Pest and its endowment, with an appeal for gifts. Continues on the next page.

transcriptions.label: Entry 554, opening lines
transcriptions.original: Dilecti in Christo Filii! Carolus Verfer Bibliopola Cassoviensis opus sub titulo: Barátságos Visgálat az Angol Egyházról, és általyában a Reformatioról praelo subjicere intendit. In optima spe, quod opus istud Scientiarum Amatoribus, et Ecclesiae Catholicae Cultoribus plene satisfacturum sit [...] Datum Szathmarini die 22a Junii 1837. Joannes mp. Episcopus Szathmariensis. Revisum per V.A.D.D.
transcriptions.english: Beloved sons in Christ! Károly Werfer, bookseller of Kassa, intends to send to press a work titled "A friendly examination of the English Church and of the Reformation in general". In the best hope that this work will fully satisfy lovers of learning and those devoted to the Catholic Church [...] Given at Szatmár, 22 June 1837. Joannes, Bishop of Szatmár, in his own hand. Revised by the vice-archdeacon of the district.

title: Entry 626 with the Eger missing-husband notice; entry 715 begins

entries.from: Josephus Linczy, vicar general
entries.abstract: At the request of Carolus Rajner, vicar of Eger, the clergy are to search for Ludovicus Szathmáry and report the result. The Eger letter is copied below it.

entries.from: Carolus Rajner, Eger
entries.abstract: A young Jewish man, son of Abraham Levi and Eva, born in Szatmár county, moved to a village in Heves county, was baptised there on 15 June 1823 as Ludovicus Szathmáry and married Catharina Tóth on 10 July of the same year. After six years and four children he left home at the start of July 1829 and never returned or wrote. His wife believes he tired of home life, went back to his former religion and returned to where he came from. Description: short, lean, long pale face, black hair, a weak left eye; speaks Hungarian, Slavic and Romanian besides his mother tongue.

entries.from: Bishop Joannes
entries.abstract: Long pastoral instruction on mixed marriages between Catholics and Protestants: the dangers the bishop sees, and how priests are to counsel couples. Continues over the next two pages.

transcriptions.label: Copy of the Eger notice, 11 July 1839
transcriptions.original: Illme &c. Juvenis quidam hebraeus Parentibus Abrahamo Levi, et Eva cujus cognomen ignoratur in Possessione [Cottus?] Szathmár Bi[...] natus. Inde ad Possessionem [Cottus?] Heves [...] delapsus, ibi anno 1823 15a Junii baptisatus, die vero 10a Julii anno eodem cum puella [...] Catharina Tóth nuptias celebravit. Exactis in Matrimonio annis 6 generatisque prolibus 4, vir hic sub initium Julii 1829 [...] domo discessit et hoc tempore nunquam remeavit, nec de ubicatione sua uxori suae ullum nuncium misit. Afflictae conditionis uxor [opinatur?] virum curarum domesticarum pertaesum ad nativam Religionem delapsum esse; locumque Originis [...] Szathmár, aut vicinos Comitatus in quibus cognatos fors habet, repetiisse [...] mentionatum virum, a tempore suscepti baptismi nomine Ludovici Szathmáry vocitatum [...] Est vir hic staturae parvae, macilentus, oblongae pallidae faciei, nigricomus, ad sinistrum oculum lippus, loquiturque praeter nativam, linguas hungaricam, slavicam ac valachicam. Agriae 11a Julii 1839. Carolus Rajner mp.
transcriptions.english: Most Illustrious Sir, etc. A certain young Hebrew, born to Abraham Levi and Eva (her surname is not known) in a village of Szatmár [county]. Having drifted from there to a village in Heves [county], he was baptised there on 15 June 1823, and on 10 July of the same year he married a girl [...], Catharina Tóth. After six years of marriage and four children, this man left home at the beginning of July 1829 and has never since returned, nor sent his wife any word of where he is. The wife, in her distress, [believes?] that her husband, weary of household cares, has lapsed to his native religion and gone back to his place of origin in Szatmár, or to the neighbouring counties where he may have relatives [...] the said man, called Ludovicus Szathmáry since his baptism [...] He is a man of short stature, lean, with a long pale face, black-haired, bleary in the left eye, and he speaks, besides his native tongue, Hungarian, Slavic and Wallachian. Eger, 11 July 1839. Carolus Rajner, in his own hand.

object.made_by: A notary, on the vendor's declaration, in or just before November 1966.
object.kept: The original stays in the notary's records; copies go to the parties and to the land registry (recalled, not sourced).

entries.from: Compiled family-tree chart (derivative source, author unknown)
entries.abstract: A printed family-tree chart, in colour, titled 'Rodostrom rodiny Javorovej' (family tree of the Javor family), with the word 'náhľad' (preview) stamped across it several times. About 250 name boxes in eight or nine generations, a coat of arms, eleven photographs and two churches. At this size only the lowest three generations and the photograph captions can be read at all. No Duska is legible anywhere on it. One ancestor is legible in part: Mary D[an]ko or D[em]ko, born 1906, died 199[?], whose box appears to give a birthplace in the U.S.A. and a line naming Vysoká nad Uhom. Her parents' boxes read Andrej D[..]ko and Mária M[...]ová, both with Vysoká nad Uhom. The younger generations are living people and are not abstracted here.

transcriptions.label: The one photograph caption that bears on either line, as far as it can be read. Square brackets mark doubtful letters.
transcriptions.original: Mary D[an]ko [or D[em]ko] 1906 - 199[?]
transcriptions.english: Mary Danko or Demko, 1906 to 199[?]. The Demko agent reads a 1991 on the chart as the death year of her son, and the last figure of hers as unclear. The surname has five letters, begins with D and ends in -ko; the two in the middle cannot be told apart at this size. The image is not published because the chart shows living people with their dates of birth. Its file name and SHA-256 are given so that the copy can be checked.

entries.from: Baptism register, Roman Catholic, Senné
entries.abstract: 'Worth remembering. The series of parish priests of the church of Szenna, as far as it could be dug out of old documents, the registers especially, after the church was recovered from the Calvinists in 1718.' Twenty-six priests follow, from Adamus Petrik to Georgius Balás (1850 to 1886), among them Stephanus Rácz, 1831 to 1841. Under Balás: windows repaired, a new organ bought; on 28 October 1865 at eleven at night something was destroyed by fire 'through a malicious man'; a bell was blessed on 20 July 1871 by Bishop László Bíró in honour of St Ladislaus, with a bell for Solymos dedicated to St Christopher. Then, in later hands: Julius Buzinkay made interim administrator; Stephanus Rusznák named administrator on 4 October 1886, invested 1887, died 3 May 1892; Buzinkay took the place on 24 July 1892 and was invested on 7 November 1894. The image carries a microfilm target reading 'Whole Volume'. Much of the lower half is at the limit of legibility and is given only in outline.

entries.from: Parish marriage register, page image (original record)
entries.abstract: Page 16 of a printed Hungarian marriage register, entry 3 of 1892. Married on 18 January 1892: András Duska, cottar, born at Szenna, living at a place read as [Hrabó?], Roman Catholic, 24 years old, bachelor; and Anna Nyemcsik, born at Szenna, living at Szenna 22, Roman Catholic, 19 years old, spinster. His parents: György Duska, Roman Catholic, farmer, of Szenna, and Anna Krak, Greek Catholic, of Tiba. Her parents: János Nyemcsik, Roman Catholic, cottar, of Szenna, and Erzsébet Hresko, Roman Catholic, of Szenna. Witnesses: András Dzvonyik, farmer; György Duska, cottar, of Szenna. Officiant: István Rusznák, dean and parish priest. Banns called three times. The ages fit the baptisms in hand: Andreas Duska of [1868] and Anna Nyemcsik of 24 August [1872]. The entries above it on the page are a widower of Nagyszeretva and a servant from Zemplén; neither concerns the line. [B-040, on a second look at the form: the groom's residence, where a house number would stand, reads 'Hrabó'. The census of 1930 lists a farmstead Hrabov belonging to Senné, so he was living on that farm, as a servant would. The word after Anna Krak's name reads 'Deba' [?] at this viewing; it was read 'I[sk]e' [?] before. A second witness is György Duska, Roman Catholic cottar of Szenna.] [B-057: the place after Anna Krak's name. I read it as 'I[sk]e' with a question mark at B-022 and, on a second look at B-040, as 'Deba' with another. The owner's hired researcher read 'Tiba' in January 2022 (D-015-12, opened only now). On an enlargement of a PNG of the same picture the word is Tiba: a looped T, i, b, a. The reading is the translator's, checked by me, and is marked so.]

entries.abstract: A two-page spread of a handwritten burial register with Hungarian headings: date of death and of burial, name, age in years, months and days, illness, and manner of burial. The surnames on it (Kenderes, Kudrócs, Knyezso, Dzvonyik, Kolyibás) are those of the Reformed baptisms of Solymos in folder F-007, so this is taken to be the Reformed burial book of the same place; the image carries no title. Two entries name the family. Under 1833, no. 3: György Dusko, buried 27 February, aged 29. Under 1838, no. 2: Pál Duska, buried in May, aged 68; the illness reads as dropsy (vízibetegség) and he was buried 'with a sermon' (tanítással). The image is small and the writing is at the limit of what it will bear: names and ages are read, days and causes are doubtful. Pál Duska, born about 1770, is the oldest person of the surname in the archive. [B-048: the strips cut from this book give more. György Dusko died on 26 February [1833] of dropsy (D-013-81); Pál Duska died on 7 June 1838, not in May (D-013-96).]

entries.from: Newspaper report (derivative source, printed far from the event), as a print from a newspaper archive
entries.abstract: A one-page print of a clipping from an Ohio newspaper, the Telegraph-Forum of Bucyrus, 17 January 1911, page 4, read in full at B-026. A report from Niobrara, Nebraska, dated 16 January: the gas lighting plant of the Hubbard hotel exploded and killed M. W. Kimball, Annie Duska, Kenneth Kindall and R. F. Crosby; four women were rescued from the fire, which burned the hotel. Nothing in it says where she came from, how old she was or whose kin she was. A Nebraska paper of the same week names the hotel's owner as Michael Kendall and lists among the dead 'Ann Duseka, a cook' (lead L-021), so the Ohio wire copy garbled at least one name and her surname is spelled two ways. The file is held because its footer carries the owner's account name on the newspaper site; the report itself is transcribed here whole.

entries.from: Urbarial table (original record, small image)
entries.abstract: The second page of the table for Solymos, a village of the first class, where a full holding is 20 holds of arable and 10 mowers of meadow. It carries the running total forward, then lists serfs 27 to 29, housed cottars 1 to 9 and sub-cottars 1 to 8, all of the first landlord. The owner's file name says an 'Andref Duska' is here. The only András on the page is sub-cottar no. 8, and his surname is read here as [B]utka, not Duska: the first letter is not the D the same clerk writes in 'Duska Mihály' on the next page, and there is a t where the s should be. Housed cottar no. 9, György, has the same surname, and he cannot be the György Duska who is housed cottar no. 10 on the next page. The image is small and the reading is low, so this is a hypothesis (H-058), not a finding. The printed columns are: name; size of the holding as a fraction of a full one; house plot in Pozsony measures; arable in holds; meadow in mowers; days of labour a year with draught animals, or instead days by hand; the ninth; then yearly dues: rent in florins, firewood in cords, spinning in pounds, clarified butter in icce, capons, chickens, eggs.

entries.from: Cemetery database record (derivative; a later keying of the burial register)
entries.abstract: A printout in French from a cemetery's records system, made on 2 January 2022. Deceased: Duska, given name written Mikalis. Date of birth 28 November 1890. Spouse: Anna Hancosek. Section FT, plot 01965. Received on 28 November 1965; a wooden coffin; the family attended the burial. The dates of death, funeral and burial all hold the value 1 January 1100, which is the system's stand-in for 'not entered'. Parents, place of death and the cemetery's own name are not on the page. The received date falls on his 75th birthday and its year repeats the plot number, so it may be a real date or a made-up one; the birth date is the only date here that can be checked, and it matches a baptism in the archive to the day: Miklós Duska, born 28 November 1890 at Szenna 6 (D-009-84). [B-049: a society's index names the cemetery, Notre-Dame-des-Neiges, with the same section, number and reception date (D-013-100).] [B-053: the cemetery explains that FT means 'fosses temporaires', common graves, with the lot numbered for the year of arrival, and that it kept almost no dates of birth before the 1980s (D-014-08). The birth date printed here may therefore have been worked out by the records system from an age, 75, and the day of arrival; that is not known either way.]

entries.from: Printed map (published source)
entries.abstract: A printed colour map of Ung county, drawn by Pál Gönczy, at 1:380,000, with relief, rivers, marsh, roads, the railway and the four districts outlined in red. It gives the county's area as 3,052.84 square kilometres and its population as 135,247, which dates it to the 1890s. For this archive it shows three things. Solymos and Szenna are neighbours, about 4 km apart by the map's scale, with marsh between them. The red district line runs between them: Solymos, Jesztreb, Rebrin and Gézsény lie in the Szobránc district, and Szenna, Pályin, Viszoka and Csicser in the Kapos district. And Lasztomér, the home of the carpenter János Demko's wife, lies just over the county line in Zemplén. Any record kept by district, a census among them, will have the two villages in different bundles.

entries.abstract: A black-and-white school map of Ung county issued for the minister of religion and education, dated 1915 in the corner, with the population of 1910 (162,089) and six districts. Someone has since added a small coloured square on every village: red across the south around Nagykapos and Csap, green across the west around Szobránc, purple through the mountains and the east, a few striped or dotted. The image has no key to the colours; by where they fall they look like the main language of each village (Hungarian, Slovak, Ruthenian), and that is this agent's inference, not something the map says. Solymos, Ungszenna, Rebrény, Gézsény and Magasrév are green; Csicser is red. Two names matter here. Szenna is 'Ungszenna', the form the Senné register takes up between 1903 and 1906. And where the older map has Viszoka, this one has Magasrév: the birthplace written on the Demko agent's 1906 record is Viszoka under its new name.

provenance.archive: family papers; not an archive record
provenance.book: see the title
provenance.obtained: From the owner's folder 'AAAA Unclassified', through the Sorter's pile 'to-duska' in the private repository at commit 2bea03e (Sorter batch S-B-013). A phone photograph of a paper original in the family's keeping.

entries.from: Original document, photograph
entries.abstract: A typed and signed Québec government form, the declaration of a civil marriage. On 11 October 1984, at the Palais de Justice in Montréal, Kevin Duska, single, born in Montréal in 1962, married Lyne Lefebvre, single, born in Montréal on 4 July 1964, French-speaking. The groom's father is entered as Steve Duska, born in Czechoslovakia, and Steve J. Duska signs as a witness. This is the first document in the archive for the link between Kevin's father and his grandfather Štefan. The bride was Kevin's mother; he states that she has died, so her name and the marriage are shown (S-000-10). entries.from: Original document, photograph
entries.abstract: A printed court form, typed in. The district court at Michalovce, acting as guardianship office, file Nsl 446/37, consents on 7 October 1937 that the minor Štefan Duško, born 23 October 1929 at Senné, may emigrate in the company of his mother, Mária Dušková née Demková of Iňačovce, to Canada, to his father Michal Duško. The mother may sign the transport contract in the guardian's place. The reasons: the father asked for it, the boy will be fully provided for with him, and the escort is over 24 years old, wholly reliable, and has bound herself in writing to take him all the way. The surname is typed Duško throughout. The boy's birthday is given as 23 October; the parish certificate of 1947 has 21 October. Nothing is said of the father's age or of where in Canada he was.

entries.from: Census household sheet (original record, screen capture)
entries.abstract: A household sheet of the Czechoslovak census of 1930, printed in Slovak and Hungarian and filled in in Hungarian: Beša, district of Veľké Kapušany, house 1[0]4, owner Ignác Schwarcz, for the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Seven people, three generations. Ignác Schwarcz, house owner, born 2 March 1865, married, a merchant on his own account, in the village since January 1870. Fanny, his wife, born 8 August 1868, married in September 1886, mother of eight children of whom two are entered beside it. Lipót, their son, born 1 January 1888, married, a merchant. Hermin, their daughter-in-law, born 21 September 1894, married on 6 January 1920 and in the village from that day. entries.from: Census household sheet (original record, screen capture)
entries.abstract: House 145, owner Andrej Duška, on the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Andrej Duška, head, born 24 November 1868 at Senné, married, a farm day-labourer who can neither read nor write. Anna, his wife, born 24 August 1872 at Senné, married on 18 January 1892, mother of twelve children of whom nine are living; she can read. Juraj, their son, born 2 March 1910, single, a day-labourer. Maria Dušková, 'daughter-in-law of the head', born 15 August 1907 at Iňačovce, Greek Catholic, married on 30 January 1927 and living in Senné since that day. Štefan Duška, 'grandson', born 23 October 1929 at Senné, Roman Catholic. Maria's husband is not in the house. This is the record that names Michal Duska's parents. Štefan, born 23 October 1929, son of a Greek Catholic Maria from Iňačovce, is the Štefan of the 1937 passport and court consent, whose father was Michal. He is entered as the grandson, and his mother as the daughter-in-law, of Andrej and Anna, married 18 January 1892: the András Duska and Anna Nyemcsik of the marriage entry D-006-03, whose son Mihály was baptised on 3 July 1903 (D-009-79). Maria's date of birth here, 15 August 1907, differs from her passport's 22 August 1906; her father-in-law, who could not read, was probably the informant. [B-050: the burial book shows thirteen children and eight burials by 1918; 'twelve, of whom nine living' is to be read again from the sheet.]

title: Passenger list: Mikulas Duska, 39, and Michal Duska, 26, of Senné, arriving in Canada, [1929 or 1930]
span: [between Nov 1929 and Jul 1930, from the ages]

provenance.archive: unknown; a Canadian passenger list by its form and its naturalisation notes
provenance.book: Passenger list, ship and date not shown
provenance.obtained: From the owner's folder 'AAAA Unclassified', through the Sorter's pile 'to-duska' in the private repository at commit 73cf83d (Sorter batch S-B-017). An enlarged crop; how the owner obtained it is not recorded.

entries.from: Passenger list (original record, cropped image)
entries.abstract: An enlarged crop of a typed passenger list of men arriving in Canada, with later notes by the immigration office. Three men in a row are from Senné, Czechoslovakia, Slovak: Andrey Dzvonik, 24; Mikulas Duska, 39; and Michal Duska, 26. The ship, the port and the date are not in the crop. Against Michal an office hand has written 'Copy on O.F. 633695' and 'Nat. 22/4/40': a copy of the entry went to file 633695, and he was naturalised on 22 April 1940. That file number is the one on the Immigration Branch letter of 1937 to Mike Duska of Montréal (D-006-11, read there as 6336[93]), so this Michal is Štefan's father. Against Mikulas: 'Nat: 21/1/46'. Between the two lines a hand has written what looks like '+ Brother'; the typed relationship column has only ditto marks under 'none'. The ages date the voyage: a man born on 3 July 1903 was 26 until July 1930, and one born on 28 November 1890 was 39 from November 1929, so they sailed between late November 1929 and early July 1930, within months of Štefan's birth. A Michal born in December 1896 would have been 33. [B-053: a second, handwritten list with the same two men and ages is D-014-01.]

entries.from: Newspaper death notice (derivative, supplied by the family; print from a newspaper archive)
entries.abstract: A death notice from The Montreal Star of Saturday 2 February 1974, page 10. Mike Duska, Sr., died at the Montreal General Hospital on 31 January 1974, aged 71. He was the husband of the late Mary Demko, the father of Steve and Mike, and the grandfather of Kevin. The funeral was on Monday 4 February from the Slovak church of St. Cyril and Method, with burial in Côte-des-Neiges cemetery, where his wife's stone stands. This is Michal Duska, Ahn 8. A man born on 3 July 1903 was 70, not 71, on that day; a family's count a year out is ordinary. The notice shows a second son, Mike, not met in any earlier record; he was not on his mother's passport in 1937, so he was born in Canada after that. The 'Sr.' is for him. The page as the owner saved it prints his account name on a newspaper website and is not published; the notice itself is shown as a crop.

Also grandfather of Kevin. Resting at Moshonas and Ouimet Funeral Home, 4898 Park Ave. Service on Monday, February 4, at 10 a.m., from St. Cyril and Method Slovak Church. Interment Cote Des Neiges Cemetery. Visitation commencing February 2, at 1 p.m.

entries.from: Civil registration of marriage (original record; image held)
entries.abstract: The provincial registration of a marriage at the church of St-Alphonse d'Youville, Montréal, on 8 December 1973, after banns. The groom is Michael Duska, inspection manager, single, 35, born in Montréal on 1 December 1938, Roman Catholic, a Canadian citizen. The bride is Marie-Claire-Francine Quenneville, born in 1949; her status is not known, so she is given by name and year only and the image is held. The owner states that the groom, his great-uncle 'Mike Jr', has died (S-000-12). A boy born in Montréal on 1 December 1938 fits a couple reunited there in November 1937, and eight weeks after this wedding the death notice of Mike Duska, Sr., names a son Mike. One thing on the form is wrong on any reading: the groom's ethnic origin is typed 'Indou' and his father's birthplace 'Inde', Hindu and India. His father was born at Senné. That he is the son of Michal Duska and Maria Demko is held at 75 in 100 (H-071): the form does not name his parents.

entries.from: Census household sheet (original record, screen capture)
entries.abstract: Michal Demko, head and owner, Greek Catholic, born 28 August 1882 at Vysoká in the Veľké Kapušany district, living in Iňačovce since 19[0.]; his wife Zuzanna, born 28 April 1901 at Iňačovce, married on 3 February 1919, two children; Juraj Demko, son, born 17 September 1911; Anna Demková, daughter, born 12 November 1924; and Maria Kočišová, entered as mother-in-law, Roman Catholic, a widow, born 15 August 1863, married on 10 November 1879, three children, two living. This is the father of Maria Demko, Ahn 18: Mihály Demkó, baptised at Viszoka in August 1882. The sheet shows him with a second wife, married in 1919, when his daughter Maria was twelve, and with a son of 1911 by the first. The widow Maria Kočišová, born 1863 and married 1879, is of the right age to be Mária Knyezső, wife of Mihály Kocsis of Solymos 19 and mother of the Mária Kocsis born in 1887: his first wife's mother. Whether Zuzanna is her daughter too is not said. All of this is the Demko agent's to rule on.

entries.from: State civil registration (original record, screenshot)
entries.abstract: A state civil registration of birth on green printed paper: page 320, entry 45, made at Alsókánya on 23 August 1906. The father appeared in person and was known to the registrar. Father: Mihály Demkó, Greek Catholic, farm day-labourer, living at Solymos, born at Magasrév, aged 24. Mother: his wife, born Mária Kocsis, Greek Catholic, living and born at Solymos, aged 20. A girl, Mária, Greek Catholic, born at Solymos on 22 August 1906 at nine in the morning. Read out and explained in Slovak; signed by the registrar and by Demko Mihály. This is the birth of Maria Demko, Ahn 9: the date is the one in her passport of 1937. The coordinator asked this agent to read the record itself before relying on it further. It was read here after the Demko agent's transcription had been seen, by this agent's own mistake in the order of work, so this is a check of that reading and not an independent one. The two agree in every field.

transcriptions.english:
Household sheet. Land and county: Subcarpathian Rus, Užhorod. District: Užhorod. Commune: Nižní Domanince. House number (new): 147. Owner of the house: Šandor Durkota.
1. Šandor Durkota, owner of the dwelling, male, married, born 10 October 1895 at Jarok, Užhorod district; in the commune since 1 November 1920; home commune Nižní Domanince; Rusyn; Greek Catholic; reads and writes; farm labourer, working by the day as hired; on 16 July 1914 also a farm labourer.
2. Anna Durkotová, wife, female, married, born 18 August 1899 at Nižní Domanince and there since birth; Rusyn; Greek Catholic; reads and writes; keeps the owner's house; for 16 July 1914 the clerk wrote 'no', after first writing 'domestic service, nursemaid' and striking it out.
3. Michal Hozuščak [?], entered as 'brother' and corrected in pencil to 'brother-in-law', male, single, born 15 October 1903 at Nižní Domanince; Rusyn; Greek Catholic; reads and writes; farm labourer by the day; no occupation in 1914.
Rows 4 to 8 are blank. Coloured pencil figures across the rows are the statistical office's codes.

object.kind: A household sheet of the Czechoslovak census of February 1921, from Subcarpathian Rus
object.form: Printed two-page form headed 'Popisný hárok. Összeirási ív.' in Slovak and Hungarian, 20 numbered columns, printer's line 'Sčítanie ľudu: Tlačivo V. č.' Columns 17 to 19 ask for the person's occupation 'on 16 July 1914', which marks the first census after the war. Filled in by one hand in Czech; coloured pencil codes and stamped running numbers 307 to 309 added by the statistical office.
object.does_not_fit: The owner's file name gives the surname as Dusko or Duska; the sheet has Durkota. The form carries no date of its own: the year is from the 1914 question, from 'in the commune since 1 November 1920', and from what is recalled of when that census was taken (recalled, not sourced).
object.made_by: A census commissioner, on the household's answers.
object.kept: The state statistical office; the sheets for Subcarpathian Rus are now in the Transcarpathian state archive and online (L-022).
compared: L-022, the portal's own description of the 1921 census collection, in the owner's translation
D-011-24, a sheet of the census of 1930, which has 24 columns and no 1914 question

entries.abstract: Two rows and the headings of the form. (1) János Dusko, of a farmer's family with a full holding; Solymos, house 30; a boy of 3; cholera; died 16 September, buried 17 September; both parents alive. The year is the one before the heading '1856', so 1855. He fits the János born on 23 August [1852] to János Duska and Anna Hura, who named another son György in 1857. (2) Mihály Dusko; house 31; aged 2[9], the figure written over; stomach cramp; died 25 May 1856, buried 27 May; 'son of a farmer with a full holding'. A grown son, unmarried by the wording, born about 1827 if the age is 29. He is not the Mihály baptised in [1840].

entries.from: Genealogical society's index to cemetery records (derivative)
entries.abstract: Index entry. Deceased: Mikalis Duska. Spouse: Anna Hancosek, followed by a letter 'd' in quotation marks. Body received on 28 November 1965 at Notre-Dame-des-Neiges cemetery, Montréal; concession 1965, section FT. This names the cemetery that the printout D-006-09 (section FT, plot 01965, received 28 November 1965) does not. The 'd' also follows Mary Demko's name in her husband's entry of 1974, when she had been dead 23 years, and is absent after Mike Duska's name in hers of 1950: it is read as 'décédé(e)', the spouse already dead. So Anna Hancosek died before 28 November 1965. The concession number equals the year, and the day of reception is the man's 75th birthday by the printout; both are in two separate records and are left as coincidences.

title: Message from Notre-Dame-des-Neiges cemetery to the owner: section FT 01965 is a common grave, and three Duskas are on its books
span: undated; after the record of 2 January 2022

provenance.archive: Notre-Dame-des-Neiges cemetery, Montréal (its reply to the owner)
provenance.book: not a register
provenance.obtained: From the owner's desktop folder 'Duska Random', sent whole through chat on 13 Nov 2026. A screenshot of a message he received from the cemetery; sender's name and date are not on it.

entries.date: undated; after the record of 2 January 2022
entries.from: Cemetery correspondence (the cemetery's own statement)
entries.abstract: The cemetery writes, unsigned: 'I have sent you all the information we had on the Duskas buried in our cemetery. We have only three on record. Section FT 01965 is a common grave. The FT, temporary graves, were common graves. The dead were buried side by side in the order they reached the cemetery. The lot number is the year of arrival. Mikalis Duska arrived on 28 November 1965 and was buried in the common graves: hence FT 01965. Nothing links the dead of one concession but the year of death, and there are more than 1,000 a year for those years. I cannot give you those lists. As for dates of birth and death, before the 1980s and 1990s cemeteries recorded almost none; the parish of the funeral kept the fuller register.' The footer gives the cemetery's own web address. Three things follow. The earlier printout (D-006-09) was sent to the owner by the cemetery. Plot '1965' is not a coincidence with the year. And the cemetery says it kept almost no dates of birth then, which puts a question against the birth date on its printout (see H-060).

transcriptions.label: The rows that bear on the line, as written, with the page headings. Other rows on the page are not transcribed.
transcriptions.original: Bonjour, je vous ai envoyé toutes les informations que nous avions sur les "Duska" inhumé à notre cimetière. Nous en avons 3 seulement d'enregistrés. La section FT 01965 est une fosse commune. les FT ou Fosses temporaires étaient des fosses communes. Les défunts étaient enterrés un à côté de l'autre selon l'ordre d'arrivé au cimetière. Le numéro de lot correspond à l'année d'arrivé au cimetière. Exemple, ici, Mikalis Duska est arrivé au cimetière le 28 novembre 1965 et a été inhumé dans les fosses communes. Donc FT 01965. Il n'y a aucun lien entre les défunts d'une même concession mis-à-part l'année de décès et il y a plus de 1000 défunts par années pour ces années. Il m'est impossible de vous donner ces listes. Pour ce qui est des dates de naissances et décès, avant les année 1980 -90, presqu'aucune information n'était enregistrée par les cimetières. C'est la paroisse des funérailles qui s'occupaient de faire un registre plus élaboré. En espérant que ceci réponde à vos questions. [...] https://www.cimetierenotredamedesneiges.ca/fr/web/cnddn/contactez-nous

entries.from: Obituary (written by the grandson, the owner of this archive; printed by a funeral home and, by his word, a newspaper)
entries.abstract: Stefan 'Steve' Duska died in Montréal on Wednesday 6 June 2018, aged 88. He was the son of Michal and Maria (Demko), was born at Senné, came to Canada 'in early childhood', and retired from the postal service. His wife Joan (Leonard) died before him. He was father to Kevin, grandfather to Kevin Jr., whom he and his wife raised, and brother to Mike. Funeral mass on Wednesday 27 June 2018 at St-Brendan's, 3542 Rosemont Boulevard, Montréal; the remains to be interred afterwards at Notre-Dame-des-Neiges. The heading gives his birth as 21 September 1929. Every record made in his lifetime says October: the 21st in the parish book and on his marriage form, the 23rd on the papers of 1937. The owner wrote the obituary and says September is his own slip (S-000-19). Every relationship in the text was already in this tree from records before it was read; what is new is the day of death, the funeral, the cemetery, that his wife died first, and that his brother was living in June 2018.

transcriptions.label: The whole notice. Two given names are withheld.
transcriptions.original:
[photograph of an old man in a cap]
DUSKA, Stefan “Steve”
September 21, 1929 – June 6, 2018
Passed away peacefully in Montreal on Wednesday, June 6, 2018 at the age of 88. The son of Michal and Maria (Demko), Steve was predeceased by his wife Joan (Leonard), father to Kevin, beloved “Pompei” to grandson Kevin Jr. [a given name in brackets, withheld], brother to Mike [a given name in brackets, withheld], and friend to many others. Born in Senné, Slovakia, Steve immigrated to Canada in early childhood. After his retirement from the postal service, he and his wife raised their grandson Kevin Jr. as if he were their own son. An avid reader and a quiet man, Steve was nevertheless a prankster whose heart was filled with great humor and kindness. He will be missed dearly by all those whose lives he touched. A funeral mass to celebrate his life will be held at St-Brendan's Catholic Church (3542, Rosemont Blvd., Montreal, Qc) on Wednesday, June 27 at 11:30 a.m. The family will receive condolences starting at 10:30 a.m. His remains will subsequently be interred at the Notre-Dame-des-Neiges Cemetery.
[footer] Alfred Dallaire MEMORIA

entries.abstract: DUSKA, MICHAEL. Sex M. Status V [widower]. Date of birth 2-7-1903. Age 70. Residence Montréal. Father: DUSKA, Joseph. Mother: ', E.' Spouse: DEMKO. Date of death 31-1-1974. This is Ahn 8 by the death date, the age and the wife. Two things do not fit the registers: the birth is a day early (the baptism book has 3 July), and the father is 'Joseph' where the baptism of 1903, the census of 1930 and the marriage of 1892 all have András. The parents of a man of 70 were told to the registrar by whoever reported the death (H-093). A second capture of this entry alone came in part 3 (Mihaily_Duska_1903_deatch_record.png); it reads the same.

entries.abstract: The Slovak Republic's birth certificate, on security paper, no. 31/2005. In the book of births of the registry office, volume 5, year 1929, page 102, entry 57, is written: born 23 October 1929 at Senné, Štefan Duška, a boy. Father: Michal Duška, 26 years old. Mother: Mária Demková, 23 years old. Birth numbers, dates and places of birth of the parents and citizenship: 'neuvedené', not stated. No remarks. Issued at Palín on 5 May 2005 under the seal of the commune's registry office. This is the state's book, and it says the 23rd. The parish's book says the 21st (D-X01-01). The parents' ages fit Michal born July 1903 and Maria born August 1906. Štefan was 75 and living in Montréal when it was issued.

entries.from: Transcription by the owner of an inscription (the object is not in hand)
entries.abstract: Eight short lines typed from handwriting by someone who does not read Slovak. Put back into Slovak they are a Christmas greeting: 'Dear Duška family, much joy with the little Jesus and at the holy supper. We will be thinking of you. May the little Jesus bless you. Good health in plenty and God's blessing, wishes the Duška family.' It is from one Duška household to another, in the Slovak of eastern Slovakia, on or with an icon that by the file name was Štefan's. So the family in Montréal had kin of the same surname at home who wrote to them at Christmas. Who, when and from where, the transcript does not say; the object might. The reconstruction is mine and four words are guesses.

entries.abstract: Michael Walter Duska, 1938 to 2019, died on 14 June 2019. Husband of a second wife, who survives him. 'Predeceased by his parents, Michal Duska and Maria Demo, as well as his brother Steve and sister-in-law Joan.' He leaves a son, two stepchildren and two grandchildren, 'as well as family in Slovakia and the Philippines'. He helped found a company called Theocon; he wintered in Florida and golfed. No place of death, burial or funeral home. The mother's surname has lost its k. With the index card of his first marriage (D-015-10) this closes H-071: the Michael born in Montréal on 1 December 1938 is the younger son of Ahn 8 and Ahn 9, and he outlived his brother Štefan by a year and eight days.

entries.from: The owner's own to-do list (a compilation by the owner: every line is a prior)
entries.abstract: Despite its name the file holds nothing from a DNA test. It is the owner's list of what he did not yet know about the Duskas in January 2022, and so a picture of his tree at that date. Each line is logged as a prior and moves nothing (PR-21). Set against the records now in this archive: (1) 'One or two Miklos who came to Montreal': the strips show one Miklós Duska born at Senné in 1890 (D-015-07), and the Montréal records fit him (H-060, 87). (2) 'Did Maria Duska (1905) die in 1908': yes, born 28 May 1905 and died 12 February 1908 at Szenna 98, a daughter of Ahn 16 and 17 (K-485). (3) 'Birthdate of Janos Duska (1877)': 4 August, by a strip whose year is the owner's (K-512). (4) 'Mike Duska (1872) as potential son of Gyorgy (1852) and Erzsebet Schwarz, established via secondary sources': a Mihály was baptised on 9 November [1872] at Szenna 5 with a smudged father and the godparents of that couple (D-009-75). But the husband of Erzsébet Schwarz is not shown to be the György born in 1852, who was baptised Reformed at Solymos; the Senné burial of 1922 makes him a man born about 1845 at Senné (H-096). (5) 'Gyorgy Duska (1880) moved to the US': two Györgys were born at Szenna 6 in 1880; one died in 1885 (K-711), the other is not traced (K-455). (6) 'Erzsebet Schwarz, 1851, and parents': not in hand; she was of Alsó-Ribnicze. (7) 'Miklo Duska born about 1890 who travelled to the US in 1913': not in hand; the Miklós of Senné married on 22 January 1913 (K-578). The ninth line is withheld.

entries.from: A researcher's report to the owner (derivative; another man's search, with one source named)
entries.abstract: The same four abstracts as D-015-12, then a paragraph to the client. He sent 'the records, with translation and scans'. He 'tried to find birth record of András' and failed. He found 'Georg's birth record', the Reformed one of 1852, 'but the only source for the information that he is his father is from the Ancestry.com'. He also looked for the birth of 'Mária Demková, from Iňačovce' and could not find her. He ends with two glosses: zsellér or želiar, which he gives as cottager, is 'a special kind of peasant' with a little land who must work for bigger farmers; gazda, which he gives as farmer, is 'more of a herder typical for Carpathian mountains'. For this archive: the baptism he could not find is here (András, 24 November [1868], D-009-06), and so is hers, with the Demko agent. The claim that the György of 1852 was the father of András came from a user-built online tree, which this agent does not open; the records in hand say otherwise (H-096, and FG-47 for András's own father). Logged as a prior (PR-22).

transcriptions.label: The closing paragraph, as typed
transcriptions.original:
[The first 28 lines are the four abstracts published as D-015-12, word for word. The file then ends with this paragraph.]

Ok so I send you the records, with translation and scans. I tried to find birth record of András but I failed I atleast found Georg's birth record, but the only source for the inforamtion that he is his father is from the Ancestry.com. I also tried to find birth records of Mária Demková, from Iňačovce, but I was unable to find her. I translated term Zsellér(hung.) =Želiar as cottager but it is not 100% correct because it is specific term for Slovakia taht means special kind of peasant living having a little land, but he needs to help bigger farmers around to get more money. Same with Gazda I translated it as farmer but it is special highland farmer or more of a herder typical for Carpathian mountains.

entries.from: Raw genotype export, compared with another (the comparison is this agent's own computation)
entries.abstract: An autosomal test, as the owner said: the same Ancestry array as his own, 668,893 markers. Nothing in the file names the person; 'Steve' is the owner's file name. Laid beside the owner's own AncestryDNA file (D-016-16), same array, 636,861 autosomal markers read in both. Same genotype at 63.37 per cent, one allele in common at 33.25, opposite homozygotes at 3.38 (21,521 markers), so not parent and child and not one person. Eighteen stretches of at least 7 megabases where the two share one copy throughout, 1,106 Mb of the 2,791 Mb the markers span: 39.6 per cent of the length of the autosomes, which is 19.8 per cent of the grandson's DNA. Chromosomes 10, 20 and 22 are shared from end to end; 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 21 not at all. X chromosome: 28,789 markers, 76.8 per cent alike by chance and no long run: nothing shared, as a male line requires. Y chromosome: 1,638 markers read in both, 1,638 identical. Mitochondrial: 195 of 195 alike, which on so few and such common markers decides nothing. Read together: a man of the same Y chromosome as the owner who shares about a fifth of his DNA with him in a few very long pieces, whole chromosomes at a time. That pattern is one generation of shuffling between the two, which is a grandfather and a grandson. It is at the low end of what a grandfather gives and inside the range (H-097). [B-067: the site's own comparison (D-016-23) gives 1,567.6 cM in 23 segments, 43.7 per cent of the map, so 21.8 per cent of the DNA. My megabase figure was low: it dropped five pieces under 7 Mb, and it counted one stretch on chromosome 11 that the site does not find and that lies across the centromere. The centimorgan figure is the one to use.]

entries.abstract: GEDmatch 'One-to-Many' for the kit beginning KJ4, which the site itself heads 'matches 1:3000 for Stefan Duska': the name is on the kit, not only on the owner's file. The first 3,000 matches, the weakest at 10.2 cM. The top four are the owner's own four kits, at 1,553 to 1,559 cM in total, largest piece 125 to 150 cM, 'generations 1.6', nothing on X: the site's own measure of the grandfather and grandson link (H-097). After them there is no near relative at all. One match at 52 cM, four between 35 and 50, 44 between 25 and 35, 89 between 20 and 25, 315 between 15 and 20, and 2,543 between 10 and 15. Not one of the 2,996 other kits carries the surname Duska in any spelling, nor Demko, Krak, Nyemcsik, Hresko, Kocsis or Schwarz. Many of the surnames near the top are of Carpathian make, Slovak, Rusyn, Polish or Hungarian, on kits tested in North America: the descendants of other emigrants from the same hills. The page's footer reads 'Copyright 2026': it was copied this year, not in 2022.

entries.from: DNA segment comparison (a database's computation from two tests)
entries.abstract: GEDmatch's one-to-one autosomal comparison of the kit named Stefan Duska with the owner's kit RW4…, run in 2026 (the page is stamped 'Ver: Jun 11 2026'). 23 shared segments, 1,567.6 cM in all, which the site gives as 43.697 per cent; the largest is 174.1 cM, the whole of chromosome 10; 'estimated number of generations to MRCA = 1.6'. 139,835 markers used. Chromosomes 10, 20 and 22 are shared from end to end and 1, 4, 12, 14, 17 and 19 for most of their length; chromosomes 3, 5 and 11 not at all. This is the site's version of the comparison I made from the two raw files at B-063 (D-016-17), and it corrects mine in three ways. It finds five short pieces, on chromosomes 7, 8, 9 (two) and 21, that my floor of 7 megabases threw away. It finds nothing on chromosome 11, where I had an 11 Mb stretch: mine lay across the centromere, where markers vary little, and was not real. And it measures in centimorgans, the proper unit: 43.7 per cent of the map on one copy is 21.8 per cent of the grandson's DNA, not the 19.8 I gave from megabases. Every long piece agrees in place and length.

entries.abstract: GEDmatch's 'Are your parents related?' run on the kit named Stefan Duska at 04:52 UTC on 14 November 2026; the owner pasted the text and sent the page as a PDF. It looks in one person's DNA for stretches where both copies are the same, which is what the child of cousins carries. Result: largest segment 0 cM, total above 7 cM 0 cM, 'no shared DNA segments found'. So Michal Duska of Senné and Maria Demko of Iňačovce, Ahn 8 and Ahn 9, were not near cousins. That bears on one thing in the two trees: each has a Hresko woman two generations above them, Erzsébet Hresko alias Minarcsin of Szenna on the Duska side and Mária Hreskó of Viszoka on the Demko side. Had those two been sisters, Michal and Maria would have been second cousins, and their son would be expected to show some such stretches (H-098).

entries.abstract: The owner's autosomal match list at a second company: 3,804 people. First on it is a kit under the name Duska, 1,566.58 cM, longest block 246.62 cM, which the owner has marked 'Grandfather': Štefan's AncestryDNA file, transferred on 5 January 2022, the day after it was downloaded. That is a third measure of the same link (GEDmatch gave 1,567.6 cM) and the company reads his Y chromosome, from the chip, as R-Z92, which is the trunk the owner's own branch grows from. After him nobody is close: the next match is 73.65 cM and five reach 50. The company has sorted 217 matches as 'Paternal'. On what linked relatives that sorting rests cannot be seen from the file, so it is taken as a pointer and no more. Among the 217, after Štefan, the largest is 24.96 cM. Three things in the list bear on the two trees. One: a match of 20.18 cM (longest block 12.07), sorted Paternal, gives 32 surnames of ancestors and one of them is Nyemcsik, spelled as the priest of Szenna spelled it; the same person is on Štefan's GEDmatch list at 32.2 cM. Štefan's father's mother was Anna Nyemcsik (H-099). Two: the largest Paternal match after Štefan bears a surname of the Demko form; that is for the Demko agent. Three: one match of 14.48 cM lists Hrisko and one of 9.68 cM lists Hresko, each among dozens of other names; noted, no weight. No match lists Duska, Demko, Krak or Kocsis among ancestral surnames, and no village of either tree is named. The surname checks were run by program over the whole list; the rows outside the Paternal sorting, which are the owner's other grandparents' sides, were not read.

entries.from: DNA analysis report (a testing company's export for one kit)
entries.abstract: The grandfather's own match list at FamilyTreeDNA: the one file of nine in this delivery that is his. Its name carries a kit number one above the owner's. 1,946 matches, three quarters of them dated 5 January 2022, the day the kit was loaded. This is the best list in the folder, because every match on it is on Štefan's side and so on one of the two trees. First is the owner, 1,566.58 cM. Second is the nearest relative of Štefan found in any database: 106.07 cM, longest block 35.56 cM, a second-to-fourth cousin by the company's range, bearing a surname of the Demko form. The same person is 24.96 cM to the owner. That is the Demko agent's (L-035). Third: 51.22 cM, longest block 27.51 cM, whose only listed ancestral surname is Mulicak, a name in neither tree (L-036). Then nine more of 29 to 42 cM. What the matches' own lists of ancestral surnames say, 620 of them being filled in. Nyemcsik: once, the match of H-099, here 34.06 cM (20.18 cM to the owner; 32.2 cM to Štefan on GEDmatch). Dusko: once, written as the pair 'Dusko/Hornyak' in a list made of such pairs, by a match of 9.35 cM in one piece. This archive has two Duska men with Hornyák wives, both at Szenna (FG-25, FG-64). That is H-100. Demko: twice (17.9 and 14.64 cM), besides Demkowicz and Demkiv once each. Tirpák: twice (22.93 and 15.3 cM), and one match bears it as a surname (12.51 cM). Hriczko: twice (20.11 and 10.27 cM). Hornyák: four times. One match of 21.49 cM bears the surname Béres, the name of the first wife of György Duska of house 6 (H-085); it is a common name and nothing rests on it. Krak, Kocsis, Hresko and Minarcsin: not once. No village of either tree is named. Checks on the other files. Of the 213 matches the company sorts to the owner's father's side (D-016-32), 212 are on this list, so that sorting is Štefan's side and nothing else. Twelve matches share X with Štefan, the largest 23 cM twice: his mother's side. One of the owner's five deep-tested Y matches also shares 9.87 cM with Štefan, and one other man on the branch above the owner's (R-Y4459) shares 15.82 cM; at that size and that depth of branch, chance is enough to explain both.
